messages:
Aisha: throwing an idea out: what if the gateway maintained a short-lived per-request "tail window" for streaming responses and used a coordinated "soft-fallback" decision when upstreams hit transient failures?
Miguel: curious. concretely, how is "soft-fallback" different from normal retries?
Aisha: two differences: 1) we don't immediately reissue backend attempts for client-visible streaming gaps; 2) we can surface a resume token so clients can reconnect and pick up without duplicate side effects.
Samir: big +1 on resume token, but need strong boundaries. must avoid holding open resources beyond SLAs. propose strict TTL and per-tenant byte caps.
Aisha: agreed. sketch of flow: 
```
1) proxy receives streaming request -> forwards to upstream A.
2) if upstream responds but then errors mid-stream and circuit open: 
   - if tail-buffer has data and meets policy: send trailer with Resume-Token and 202-like acceptance, keep tail for T seconds.
   - else set Retry-Hint=no-retry and return appropriate 5xx/fallback.
3) client can re-open with If-Resume-Token header to continue.
```
Miguel: what's the contract for idempotency? If client reconnects and upstream actually processed the full request, will we double-run?
Aisha: need a lifecycle: resume-token binds to proxy-side buffered tail and an idempotency marker from upstream when available. If the upstream processed, resume attempt becomes a no-op. we should expose a Resume-Status in the handshake.
Samir: on implementation: prefer evict-on-overcommit policy rather than blocking new requests. metrics to watch: resume.tokens.issued, resume.tokens.expired, resume.buffer.evicted, retry_shaper.suppressed.
SRE: operational concerns: don't let feature cause cascading increase in connections to upstreams. add a token-limiter and circuit-aware shaping: if CB is open for an upstream cluster, suppress retries for N seconds and prefer resume flow.
Miguel: header/handshake idea: 
```
# Proxy -> client trailers
X-RW-Resume-Token: rtk-<hex>
X-RW-Resume-TTL: 3s
X-RW-Resume-Size: 12KB
Trailer: X-RW-Resume-Token

# Client -> proxy when re-opening
If-Resume-Token: rtk-<hex>
```
Aisha: also propose control-plane flags: per-tenant buffer cap, global buffer pool, and a fast-disable flag for canary rollback. infra-bot: feature-flag resume_stream_tail created (default off).
infra-bot: rollout note: metric hooks added: resume.tokens.issued (counter), resume.buffer.bytes (gauge), resume.buffer.evictions (counter).
Samir: billing note: buffer time is pro-rated; mark buffered segments as transient in traces so billing pipeline can dedupe. not charging twice if replay occurs.
SRE: runbook snippet: if resume.buffer.evictions spikes > 1% of requests over 5m -> disable feature and open incident. also watch retry_shaper.suppressed_ratio > 0.2.
Miguel: implementation plan: lightweight in-memory ring buffer per-connection aggregated per-tenant; persistence not needed. default TTL 3s, default tenant cap 256KB. can tune.
Aisha: open questions: 1) should we allow resume across regions? likely no, token bound to region. 2) should tokens be single-use? yes, single-use reduces complexity.
Samir: note on security: token must be opaque and HMAC-signed with region key to avoid replay across clusters.
SRE: add alerting and dashboards during canary: time-to-first-resume, resume-success-rate, buffer-eviction-rate.
Aisha: thanks. I'll turn this into a short RFC with sequence diagrams and a proposed API contract + runbook. meeting next Thu to review. :rocket:
